newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru's lawyers plan to quit - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru's lawyers plan to quit - sources.

text.p: Court-appointed lawyers defending the leader of the Japanese doomsday cult accused of the Tokyo subway gas attack plan to resign on Thursday, legal sources said.

The sources said the lawyers' resignations, which were unlikely to be accepted by the Tokyo District Court, were in protest at what they regard as the hurried nature of cult leader Shoko Asahara's murder trial.

Osamu Watanabe, head of the 12-member team of lawyers, last week told a news conference the team had asked for a two-month recess in the trial of Asahara, head of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect).
Asahara is on trial for the March 1995 nerve-gas attack on the Tokyo subway system, which killed 12 and harmed 6,000 people, as well as a number of other murder, drugs and weapons charges.
Watanabe also wanted the number of Asahara's court sessions in the 10-month-old trial cut from four to three per month.
The court has refused Watanabe's demands. The sources said the court was also expected to reject the resignations.
If the court rejects the resignations, the lawyers may boycott Asahara's next session, scheduled for March 13, the sources said.
In Japan, a court session for a murder suspect cannot be held without lawyers present.
Asahara's trial has been marked by controversy, including his repeated outbursts against judges, witnesses, prosecutors and even his own lawyers.
The outbursts have led to Asahara's expulsion from court on several occasions.
A spokesman for the Tokyo District Court refused to comment on the case.
